R0054.title: Malicious Returns
R0054.definition: A buyer returns goods not for legitimate reasons, but to disrupt the seller or platform, or to gain improper benefits.
R0054.description: A buyer purchases high-value, large, or scarce items with the intent to disrupt or damage, then initiates a return as soon as the goods arrive or before they arrive, causing financial loss or reputational damage to the seller through high return rates. Alternatively, a buyer uses the 7-day no-questions-asked return policy on high-value items after using them, causing depreciation, then colluding with insiders to purchase the depreciated item.
R0054.influence: Consumes the seller's profits, inventory, reputation, or supply chain costs.

references.title: Buyer Uses Courier Tracking Number for Malicious Refund of Nearly 40,000 Yuan, Faces Fraud Charges

observables: A buyer places orders for large or scarce items and initiates frequent returns within a short window, with a return rate far above average
High-value items are returned under the 7-day no-questions-asked policy after being used, showing clear depreciation
Return tracking numbers are anomalous or refund requests are filed before the goods have arrived
The same buyer or linked buyers concentrate returns against a specific seller with tightly clustered timing

R0054-001.title: Bulk Refunds
R0054-001.definition: Placing bulk orders through the same or different accounts and initiating illegitimate bulk returns or refunds.
R0054-001.description: Using automated or manual means to place large numbers of orders or high-value orders, then bulk-canceling and requesting refunds, maliciously consuming supply chain costs or causing the seller's return rate to rise.
R0054-001.influence: Disrupts the seller's normal operations, causing supply chain losses or a drop in ratings and rankings.

references.title: Tai'an Announces Typical Cases of Combating New Telecom and Cyber Crimes

observables: The same account or a cluster of linked accounts files a large volume of refund requests in a short window
Refund requests follow a mechanical timing pattern, with highly regular intervals between order placement and refund
High-value orders are placed in bulk and then refunded in bulk, causing a sharp spike in the return rate
Refund amounts cluster near discount or promotion tier thresholds

R0054-002.title: Return Fraud
R0054-002.definition: A buyer returns a counterfeit, used, empty, incomplete, or substitute item instead of the original purchased product.
R0054-002.description: The returned item is not the actual item that was shipped — such as returning a counterfeit or a different product (buy A, return B). The quantity of returned items differs from what was actually shipped, including empty packages.
R0054-002.influence: Causes financial loss to the platform or seller.

references.title: Receiving Genuine Goods but Returning Counterfeits: Does It Constitute Fraud - Qionglai People's Procuratorate
Buying Real Goods, Returning Fakes: Man Defrauds 2.27 Million Yuan, Sentenced to 11 Years - Guangming Daily
Buy Genuine, Return Fake: Court Sentences to 3 Years with 4 Years Probation - Nanchang Donghu District People's Court

observables: The inbound shipment weight on return does not match the outbound shipment weight, with discrepancies beyond logistics error margins
The SN or anti-counterfeit code of the returned item does not match the shipped item or is a high-quality counterfeit
Return packages are empty or missing accessories, and return senders cluster around a small number of accounts
A buy-A-return-B pattern: the returned item's category differs markedly from the original order

R0054-003.title: Flash Return Arbitrage
R0054-003.definition: Placing an order to receive gifts, vouchers, or discounts, then immediately canceling the order to extract the benefits.
R0054-003.description: A targeted fraudster may stockpile large numbers of accounts and monitor platform or merchant promotions in real time. Upon finding a profitable opportunity, they place bulk orders via automation, extract coupons, gifts, or other benefits, and then immediately cancel the orders for profit.
R0054-003.influence: Causes financial loss to the platform and sellers.

references.title: Exploiting Platform Flash Refund Rules to Fleece E-commerce: Student Sentenced for Refund Without Return - The Paper
Malicious Refunds Exploiting E-commerce Settlement Rules Constitutes Fraud - Shandong High People's Court

observables: The interval between order placement and refund is extremely short (minutes), and refunds cluster right after coupons or gifts are claimed
Accounts place bulk orders the instant a marketing campaign begins, extract the benefits, and immediately cancel the orders
During campaigns, the return rate and the coupon-claim rate for the same device or account cluster are severely inverted
The flash refund channel is used at high frequency, with returns concentrated on orders that already issued coupons

R0054-004.title: Malicious Refusal of Delivery
R0054-004.definition: A buyer refuses to accept goods for retaliatory or disruptive purposes, occupying or consuming the seller's supply chain resources and causing financial loss.
R0054-004.description: A typical malicious attack scenario: a buyer purchases large items such as appliances, electronics, construction materials, or tires, then goes unreachable or refuses delivery when the courier arrives, occupying and consuming the seller's supply chain costs.
R0054-004.influence: Maliciously refused large items incur round-trip reverse logistics, warehousing, and depreciation costs of tens to hundreds of yuan per order; goods stranded at end delivery points tie up inventory and capital, and large-scale refusals push up the seller's return-rate metrics and trigger platform demotion and traffic limits, also degrading delivery timeliness and stock availability for legitimate users.

references.title: Ministry of Public Security Announces Top 10 Financial Black-Grey Market Crime Cases

observables: A buyer goes unreachable or refuses delivery for large items such as appliances, electronics, or building materials at the dispatch stage
The same shipping address or linked accounts repeatedly order large items and refuse delivery, with reverse logistics costs concentrated
Refusals cluster after the goods have arrived at the last-mile outlet, with no legitimate reason given
The seller's return rate and refusal rate spike abnormally in specific categories
